PRIMARY RESULT — Pearson correlation coefficient between gene length and mean expression (across samples) for protein-coding genes in CD14 immune cells, per the locked literal definition (per-gene mean = arithmetic mean of raw batch-corrected counts over all 132 CD14 samples; 19,942 protein-coding genes; scipy.stats.pearsonr):

r = 0.031694 (≈0.0317, 6 significant digits)
p = 7.59e-06
n = 19,942 genes
r² = 0.001005

Interpretation: a very weak positive correlation on the raw-count scale (r² ≈ 0.1%).

Clearly-labeled sensitivity variants (NOT the headline; for choosing the final headline):
(a) Pearson(log2(mean+1) vs Length): r = 0.280389, p < 1e-16, r² = 0.078618 (n = 19,942)
(b) Pearson(mean-of-log2(count+1) across samples vs Length): r = 0.277338, p < 1e-16, r² = 0.076917 (n = 19,942)

Zero-mean gauge: 1,849 of the 19,942 protein-coding genes (9.27%) have mean expression = 0 across the 132 CD14 samples; including or excluding them changes the raw-scale r modestly — under the locked protocol they are included.

Per the approved protocol, the default/final answer is the PRIMARY raw-count value: r = 0.031694. Executed analysis script is retained at analysis/compute_correlation.py with console output at analysis/compute_correlation.out and machine-readable results at analysis/results.json; executed_analysis is set true in payload.
